tool.name: query_granola_meetings
tool.title: Query meetings
tool.description:
Query Granola about the user's meetings using natural language. Returns a tailored response with inline citation links in mark  (e.g. [[0]](url)) that reference source meeting notes.

IMPORTANT: The response includes numbered citation links to specific Granola meeting notes. These citations MUST be preserved in your response to the user — they provide transparency and allow the user to verify information by clicking through to the original notes.

This tool is slow: an AI agent behind it searches and reads the user's notes before answering. Prefer a faster tool when it can answer the question:
- list_meetings: find meetings by date range
- get_meetings: read notes for meetings whose IDs you already have

When to use:
- User asks about what was discussed, decided, or action-items from meetings
- User asks about follow-ups, todos, or commitments from recent meetings
- User references 'Granola notes' or 'meeting notes'

When NOT to use:
- User is asking about calendar scheduling or upcoming events
- User explicitly asks for a specific meeting by ID (use get_meetings instead)

Prioritize using query_granola_meetings over list_meetings/get_meetings for open-ended or natural language queries about meeting content.

If this tool does not find a requested detail, meeting summaries may have omitted it. Use list_meetings/get_meetings to identify the most relevant meetings, then get_meeting_transcript only where that meeting's workspace permits transcript access. If access is denied, report that limitation; do not retry through another tool or conclude the information was never discussed.

tool.name: list_meetings
tool.title: List meetings
tool.description:
List the user's Granola meeting notes within a time range. Returns meeting titles, metadata, and note URLs.

IMPORTANT: For short-term questions about recent meeting details, prefer using query_granola_meetings instead.

When to use:
- User asks to list their meetings
- User asks about action items, decisions, or summaries from meetings over a longer or specific date range
- User asks about content from their meeting transcripts
- User references 'Granola notes' or 'meeting notes' or 'transcripts'

When NOT to use:
- User is asking about upcoming calendar events or scheduling
- User wants to create/modify calendar invites

Filtering:
- Omit workspace_only and involvement to return every meeting the user is allowed to access
- For 'my meetings' or meetings the user was involved in, set both involvement conditions to true; true conditions combine using OR
- Set captured_by_me to true for meetings whose Granola notes the user captured, or false to exclude them
- Set listed_as_participant to true for meetings where the user is a known participant, or false to exclude them
- False involvement conditions are exclusions and combine with the positive conditions using AND; omit a condition to ignore it
- For Team Space or public workspace meetings, set workspace_only to true
- workspace_only and involvement combine using AND

Use get_meetings to retrieve detailed meeting content after identifying relevant meetings.
Use list_meeting_folders to discover folder IDs, then pass a folder_id to list meetings within a specific folder.

folder_id.description: Optional folder ID to list meetings from a specific folder. Requires a paid Granola plan. Use list_meeting_folders to discover folder IDs.

custom_end.description: ISO date for custom range end (required if time_range is 'custom').

time_range.description: Time range to query meetings from.

captured_by_me.description: True includes meetings whose Granola note was captured by the connected user; false excludes them; omit to ignore who captured the note. This identifies the note owner, not necessarily the meeting organizer.

listed_as_participant.description: True includes meetings where the connected user's email appears in Granola's known participant metadata; false excludes them; omit to ignore participant metadata. Participant metadata can be incomplete and does not prove attendance.

involvement.description: Optional involvement filter. Conditions set to true form an OR inclusion group. Conditions set to false are exclusions applied using AND. Omitted conditions are ignored.

custom_start.description: ISO date for custom range start (required if time_range is 'custom').

workspace_only.description: Set to true only when the user explicitly asks for Team Space, public workspace, or workspace-visible meetings. Omit to search every meeting the user is allowed to access.

tool.name: get_meetings
tool.title: Read meetings
tool.description:
Get detailed meeting information for one or more Granola meetings by ID. Returns private notes, AI-generated summary, attendees, metadata, and note URLs.
Does not return transcripts. Notes and summaries can omit details that were discussed.
If a detail is missing, use get_meeting_transcript on the most relevant meetings only where that meeting's workspace permits transcript access. If access is denied, report that limitation; do not retry through another tool or conclude it was never discussed.
Use this when you already have specific meeting IDs (e.g. from list_meetings results). For open-ended questions about meeting content, use query_granola_meetings instead.

tool.name: get_meeting_transcript
tool.title: Read meeting transcript
tool.description:
Get the full transcript for a specific Granola meeting by ID. Returns only the verbatim transcript content, not summaries or notes.
Transcript blocks separate audio source (Microphone/System audio) from speaker identity. Participant attribution and user-confirmed names are preserved. Desktop diarization is omitted; mobile/imported transcripts can retain Speaker A/B/... labels for unnamed voices. Recording context identifies the document owner as the recorder for native recordings, not as the speaker. Missing recorder data stays unknown; the current viewer is not substituted. Channels and room labels may include multiple people. Older preformatted transcripts keep their original labels.
Requires access to the meeting and transcript access permitted by that meeting's workspace. Use this for exact quotes or when query_granola_meetings/get_meetings does not surface a requested detail, such as a person, example, or explanation. Start with the most relevant meetings; a detail missing from summaries may still be in the transcript. If access is denied, report that limitation and do not retry through another tool. For general summaries or action items, start with query_granola_meetings or get_meetings.

tool.name: get_account_info
tool.title: Get account info
tool.description:
Get the email, active workspace, joined workspaces (names and IDs), and effective note-access scopes for the Granola account currently connected to this MCP session.

Workspace membership does not imply MCP access to its meetings.

When to use:
- User asks 'who am I signed in as?', 'which Granola account is this?', or 'what's my email?'
- User suspects they connected the wrong Granola account
- User asks which workspaces they belong to or mentions another workspace
- Meeting results may be missing because the wrong workspace is active
- Meeting results may be incomplete or empty because of the user's Granola plan or workspace MCP access controls
- Before performing actions, to confirm identity if the user references a specific account

mcp_note_access.scopes contains the note categories this connection can search:
- personal: notes the connected user owns, notes shared directly with them, and notes accessible through private folders
- public: notes accessible through workspace-visible Team Space folders
- Both scopes means both categories can be searched. These scopes describe access, not who captured or participated in a meeting.

_published_faq.name: How do I add Granola to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add Granola to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://mcp.granola.ai/mcp. This server requires OAuth, so complete the login prompt after you connect.

_published_faq.name: Is Granola MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 6, 2026, Granola scores 100/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan meets ChatGPT publishing checks and meets Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

_published_faq.name: How clear is Granola's MCP tool documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 6, 2026, Granola scores 84/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations. The review covers 6 of 6 discovered tools. The quality score measures documentation clarity; runtime behavior and marketplace readiness require separate checks.

_published_faq.name: What tools does the Granola MCP server provide?

acceptedAnswer.text: Granola provides these MCP tools: query_granola, list_meetings, get_meetings, and get_meeting_transcript.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to Granola?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to Granola in communication on the Manufact MCP catalog include AgentLine: Phone Numbers for AI Agents, JooVoice, OpenMail, Fleet Connected Apps, and inkbox.
Granola requires authentication. Connect it in Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor and complete the OAuth login prompt.

_published_faq.name: How can Granola improve its MCP documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: query_granola_meetings is the lowest-scoring reviewed tool at 78/100. No output schema is declared. Add one for structured results so clients can interpret returned fields. Open its review for feedback and a copyable fix prompt, then rerun the documentation review after updating your tool metadata.
